title: The Laguerre polynomial divisibility conjecture
statement:
Let $n,k\in\mathbb{N}$ and $m\in\mathbb{N}_0$. **Laguerre polynomial divisibility conjecture.** If the Laguerre polynomial $L_k$ divides the generalized Laguerre polynomial $L_n^{(m)}$, then

$$
L_n^{(m)}=L_k.
$$

The paper uses this conjecture to establish the preceding Wigner zero-set claim and reports that it is proved in several cases, while other cases remain open.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.20324

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2025).
source_name: Luís Daniel Abreu, Ulysse Chabaud, Nuno Costa Dias and João Nuno Prata, “Inverse problems for the zeros of the Wigner function”, arXiv:2504.20324 (2025).
